events.what: Tian represents the last unrepresented lattice of at most seven elements (L7/L10) as the subgroup interval [S3, PSL(2,64)]; the DeMeo–Freese–Jipsen project recomputes it in GAP and finds a smaller Sp(6,2) representation

judgement.doubts: The result itself looks sound: it is an explicit subgroup interval that GAP recomputed, and a smaller representation was found independently. The downgrade is about scope, not correctness. The bullet makes a universal claim about all finite lattices. Finishing the census of lattices with at most seven elements shows that finitely many specific lattices are representable, the same pattern as the F4 poset census. It is not a structural class or a parameter range proved by argument. Someone could still read 'all lattices with at most 7 elements' as a size-restricted case (the record's competing reading). If a later pass takes that view, the status would be partial/confirmed. The AI involvement was commit-message credits on verification tooling plus Copilot code review, so ai_role none is correct either way.

corrections.why: F4: the record says the event closes 'the last outstanding case among lattices with at most seven elements'. That means one more explicit lattice has been shown to be representable, which finishes a finite census of a universal statement about all finite lattices. That is scope 'instances', which is discarded. Nothing had resolved the problem before the snapshot, so the status is open.
F14: no surviving event, so the status is open and the direction is null.
F9: the basis quote only shows AI helping build verification tooling (commit credits) and Copilot reviewing code. Neither produced any of the mathematics, so none stands.
